introduction:
A Death Certificate in West Bengal is issued by the Municipal Corporation, Municipality, or Gram Panchayat under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act. The e-District West Bengal 2.0 portal handles online applications.

Mandatory for insurance, property mutation, bank closure, pension, and succession proceedings. Track via edistrict.wb.gov.in.
quickFacts:
Important to Know
  • Service Name: Death Certificate Registration
  • State: West Bengal
  • Official Portal: Janma-Mrityu Tathya (janma-mrityutathya.wb.gov.in)
  • Application Window: This specific process is for deaths registered within 1 to 21 days of occurrence. (Applications after 21 days fall under the Delayed Death Registration category).
documentsRequired:
Documents Required

Note: All documents must be uploaded online, and the file size for each should not exceed 250 KB.
Identity Proofs
  • Applicant's ID Proof: Aadhaar Card, EPIC (Voter ID), Khadya Sathi, Passport, etc.
  • Deceased's ID Proof: Aadhaar Card, EPIC (Voter ID), Khadya Sathi, Passport, etc.
Death & Cremation Proofs
  • Form No. 2: Scanned copy of the Death Report Form.
  • Doctor's Certificate: Death Certificate issued by the attending doctor.
  • Cremation / Burial Certificate: Proof of last rites issued by the crematorium, graveyard, or the local Gram Panchayat (for rural areas).
onlineApplication:
Method 1: Apply Online via Janma-Mrityu Tathya Portal

This process is completely online; no offline visits are required if all documents are in order.

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Visit Portal: Visit the official portal: janma-mrityutathya.wb.gov.in.
  2. Step 2: Navigate: On the top menu bar, hover over Citizen Services, select Death, and click on Apply for New Registration.
  3. Step 3: Mobile Authentication: Enter your active mobile number and click Get OTP. Enter the OTP received and click Submit OTP.
  4. Step 4 (Applicant Details): Select your relationship with the deceased, enter your name, select the ID proof type, enter the ID number, and upload your ID proof.
  5. Step 5 (Deceased Details): Select the Date of Death from the calendar, gender, age, and enter the First, Middle, and Last name of the deceased. Select their ID proof type, enter the ID number, and upload the ID proof.
  6. Step 6 (Place of Death): Select where the death occurred (Hospital, Home, or Others). If "Home" is selected, fill out the complete address details including State, District, Block/Municipality, Village/Town, and PIN Code.
  7. Step 7 (Family Information): Fill in the Mother's, Father's, and Spouse's (if applicable) information. Provide their names, mobile numbers, ID types, and ID numbers. Uploading their ID proofs is optional if not available.
  8. Step 8 (Addresses): Fill in the "Address of deceased at the time of death". If the permanent address is the same, tick the checkbox "Please check if Permanent address is same as above address".
  9. Step 9 (Informant Information): Tick the checkbox if the informant's address is the same as the permanent address. Enter the Informant's name, Designation (e.g., Asha worker, or "Other"), and their address details.
  10. Step 10 (Statistical Information): Select the deceased's Religion and Occupation from the dropdown menus. You can also add remarks if necessary.
  11. Step 11 (Upload Documents): Upload the remaining mandatory documents: Form No. 2, Doctor's Death Certificate, and the Cremation/Burial Certificate (each under 250 KB).
  12. Step 12: Submit: Review the entire form carefully and click on the Submit button at the bottom.
  13. Step 13: Acknowledgment: An Acknowledgement Number will be generated on the screen. Note this down or copy it for future tracking.
offlineApplication:
Method 2: Apply Offline

Since the video focuses only on the online method, here is the standard offline procedure for West Bengal based on current government guidelines:

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Step 1: Visit the Local Office: Visit your respective local body office. For rural areas, go to the Gram Panchayat office. For urban areas, go to the Municipality or Municipal Corporation office. (Note: Institutional deaths in government hospitals are usually registered by the hospital authorities themselves).
  2. Step 2: Request Form: Request Form No. 2 (Death Report Form) from the Registrar of Births and Deaths desk.
  3. Step 3: Fill Details: Fill out the form with accurate details of the deceased and the informant.
  4. Step 4: Attach Documents: Attach physical copies of the required documents (Doctor's Death Certificate, Cremation/Burial receipt, and ID proofs of the deceased and the applicant).
  5. Step 5: Submit: Submit the completed application to the designated officer and collect your physical acknowledgment receipt.
afterApplying:
After Applying — What Next?

Track Application Status

Go to the portal, navigate to Citizen Services -> Death -> Track Application. Enter your Acknowledgement Number and Date of Death, then click Submit to view the current status.

Download Certificate

Once your application is approved by the authorities, go to Citizen Services -> Death -> Download Certificate. Enter your Acknowledgement Number or Certificate Number and click Search. You will receive an OTP on your registered mobile number. Enter the OTP to download your digitally signed Death Certificate.
